detailed_rationale:
Indigo Paints is a differentiated Indian decorative-paints player, notable for holding roughly 80-90% share in several category-creating niche products (Metallic and Tile Coat Emulsions among them) rather than competing head-on across the full paints category. FY26 was a year of modest growth: sales grew to Rs 1,405 Cr from Rs 1,341 Cr (+4.8%) and net profit to Rs 148 Cr from Rs 142 Cr (+4.2%), but the quarterly trend improved through the year -- operating margin climbed from 14% (Jun 2025) to 22% (Mar 2026), and profit nearly doubled sequentially over that span (Rs 26 Cr to Rs 59 Cr) -- a genuine positive trajectory even though the full-year growth number looks unexciting.

The balance sheet is clean (borrowings of just Rs 21 Cr, effectively debt-free) and promoter holding is stable (~54%), with no dilution or governance flag in the data available. At a PE near 35x, the stock carries a premium multiple typical of the paints category (where Asian Paints and other listed peers have historically commanded rich valuations for brand and distribution moats), even though Indigo's own recent growth has been modest.

The Indian decorative-paints industry overall has seen intensifying competitive entry over the past few years from large diversified players expanding into paints, which is a genuine structural risk to margins and growth for smaller/niche players industry-wide; we note this as a sector-level risk factor rather than something specific we found about Indigo's own numbers, since it did not surface directly in the sources reviewed this pass.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, matching the quant score -- the improving within-year margin trend is a genuine positive, and the balance sheet is clean, but full-year growth was modest and the paints category is seeing rising competitive intensity industry-wide, so we are not inclined to go beyond Hold on the current data.
summary: Indigo Paints, known for strong positions in several niche decorative-paint categories, grew revenue and profit modestly in FY26, but margins improved meaningfully through the year (from 14% to 22% operating margin) and the balance sheet remains essentially debt-free. The broader paints industry is seeing more competitive entry from larger players, a sector-wide risk to watch. We rate it a Hold.
positive_para: Indigo holds durable, differentiated leadership (80-90% share) in several created-category paint products, is essentially debt-free, and showed a clear improving margin trend through FY26 (14% to 22% operating margin, with profit nearly doubling sequentially into Q4).
negative_para: Full-year revenue and profit growth were both modest (under 5%), below what the paints category has historically delivered in stronger years, and the broader decorative-paints industry has seen rising competitive intensity from larger diversified players over the past few years -- a structural risk to smaller/niche players' pricing power and growth that is worth monitoring even though it did not show up as a company-specific issue in this pass.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 35x earnings, the market is paying a category-typical premium multiple for paints-industry brand and distribution quality, but Indigo's own recent growth (under 5%) does not yet clearly justify that premium on its own -- the improving in-year margin trend helps the case, but we would want to see full-year growth reaccelerate into double digits before treating the multiple as comfortably earned.
